title: Chapter 10 — Refrigeration
intro: The highest-traffic category — configurations, capacity logic, feature tiers, and the five questions every refrigerator sale starts with.

sections.title: The Category That Drives Traffic
content: Refrigeration is the highest-traffic category on the floor. More customers walk in looking for a refrigerator than any other appliance. This is the category where you will spend the most time, answer the most questions, and close the most sales. Knowing refrigeration cold — every configuration, every feature tier, every installation consideration — is non-negotiable.

sections.title: Configurations: Know Every Type
content: **Top-Freezer.** The original. Freezer on top, fresh food below. Lowest price point, smallest footprint, most reliable. This is the rental property refrigerator, the garage unit, the first apartment. Capacity typically 14–21 cu ft. Brands: Amana, Frigidaire, GE, Whirlpool. Customers buying top-freezers are usually price-driven or space-constrained. Don't upsell aggressively — they know what they want.

**Bottom-Freezer.** Fresh food at eye level — no bending to reach the lettuce. Pull-out freezer drawer below. Popular with older customers and anyone who prioritizes fresh food access. Capacity 18–24 cu ft. This is the natural step-up from a top-freezer for customers who want better ergonomics without going to a French door.

**Side-by-Side.** Narrow doors (good for tight kitchens), ice and water dispenser, freezer and fridge both at eye level. Downside: neither side is wide enough for a full sheet pan or large platter. Capacity 22–28 cu ft. This configuration is declining in popularity as French doors take over, but it remains strong in kitchens where door swing clearance is limited.

**French Door.** The dominant configuration in the market. Two narrow doors on top for the fresh food section, full-width freezer drawer below. Wide shelves accommodate platters, pizza boxes, sheet pans. Most have ice and water dispensers. Capacity 20–30 cu ft. Available at every price point from $1,200 to $4,000+. This is the default recommendation for most customers doing a kitchen renovation.

**Counter-Depth.** Not a configuration — a depth specification. Counter-depth refrigerators are shallower (typically 24–25 inches deep vs 30–33 for standard depth) so they sit flush with cabinetry. They look built-in without the built-in price. Trade-off: you lose 4–6 cu ft of capacity. Every major brand offers counter-depth in French door and side-by-side. This is the most important upsell in refrigeration — the visual impact is dramatic and the customer often doesn't know it exists until you show them.

**Column Refrigeration.** Separate full-size refrigerator and full-size freezer installed side by side (or apart). No compromise — full width, full depth, full capacity for both. Premium and luxury segment: Sub-Zero, Thermador, Monogram, Miele, Dacor. Price: $8,000–$20,000+ for the pair. The customer buying columns is building a dream kitchen. This is a design sale, not a feature sale.

**Built-In.** Permanently installed, finished on the sides and top with cabinetry panels or stainless steel. Deeper than counter-depth, finished to look like furniture. Sub-Zero, Thermador Freedom, JennAir, Monogram. These refrigerators are architectural elements — they define the kitchen. Price: $8,000–$15,000+.

**Compact/Undercounter.** 24-inch wide, fits under a standard counter. Used in wet bars, butler's pantries, outdoor kitchens, offices, secondary locations. Beverage centers, wine storage, drawer refrigerators. Brands: Sub-Zero, U-Line, True Residential, KitchenAid, Bosch. This is an add-on sale — the customer is buying a primary refrigerator AND an undercounter unit.

sections.title: Key Features to Know
content: **Ice and Water Systems.** Internal dispenser (inside the door — cleaner look) vs external dispenser (on the door — more convenient). Measured fill, crushed vs cubed, some brands offer specialty ice (LG Craft Ice spheres, GE nugget ice). Filtration is a recurring revenue opportunity — remind customers to change filters every 6 months.

**Smart/Connected.** Wi-Fi enabled refrigerators can send alerts (door left open, filter reminder, temperature deviation), view inside with cameras, and integrate with smart home systems. Samsung Family Hub has a screen on the door. LG ThinQ offers remote diagnostics. Smart features matter most to younger buyers and tech-forward households.

**Temperature Management.** Dual evaporators (separate cooling for fridge and freezer — prevents flavor transfer) vs single evaporator. Sub-Zero pioneered dual compressors. Bosch has FarmFresh System. These features preserve food quality and reduce waste — a selling point for customers who buy quality groceries.

**Capacity vs Usable Space.** Advertised cubic footage includes shelf supports, door bins, and dead space. Usable capacity is always less. Show the customer the INSIDE, not the spec sheet. Adjustable shelves, split shelves, full-width deli drawers — these determine how the refrigerator lives day to day.

**Finish Options.** Stainless steel (standard), black stainless (fading in popularity), slate/matte finishes (GE, Café), custom panel-ready (luxury), Bespoke panels (Samsung). Fingerprint-resistant finishes are a selling point — ask the customer if they have kids.

sections.title: The Five Questions Every Customer Asks
content: 1. **What size do I need?** Measure the opening (width, depth, height). Standard widths: 30", 33", 36". Check door swing clearance, adjacent walls, and island proximity. Counter-depth vs standard depth is the second question inside this question.

2. **French door or side-by-side?** French door for wide shelves and kitchen flow. Side-by-side for narrow kitchens where a French door would block a walkway. Bottom-freezer if they prioritize fresh food access and don't need a dispenser.

3. **How quiet is it?** Refrigerator noise is measured in dBA but rarely published. Premium units are noticeably quieter. If the customer has an open-concept kitchen, noise matters — demonstrate the difference between a $1,200 unit and a $2,500 unit.

4. **How long will it last?** Average refrigerator lifespan is 10–15 years. Simpler units (top-freezer, fewer electronics) tend to last longer. More features = more potential failure points. Be honest about this trade-off.

5. **Is it worth the extra money?** Always answer by showing, not telling. Open the door, pull out the shelves, point to the build quality. The customer can see and feel the difference between a $1,500 refrigerator and a $3,000 refrigerator. Let the product sell itself.

sections.title: Coaching Rule
content: Stand in front of every refrigerator on your floor. Open every door. Pull out every shelf. Know the cubic footage, the price, the key differentiator, and the customer it's right for. You should be able to walk a customer to the right refrigerator in under 90 seconds based on their answers to three questions: size, configuration, and budget.
